subject: predict(fit) - how can I keep my scale?

messages.author: d1c18ef25d6c7ec3
messages.subject: predict(fit) - how can I keep my scale?
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I fitted a cfa model with lavaan and try to predict the resulting latent variables. I would like to report some descriptive statistics of these "new" variables, such as their mean, sd and correlation. However the new scale seems to be centered around the mean of 0. E.g. with a min of ~-3.5 and a max of ~3.5, instead of 1--7.
How do I keep the original scale?

Thanks
Roman

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: predict(fit) - how can I keep my scale?
parts:
On 01/28/2014 01:54 PM, Roman wrote:
> Hi everyone,
>
> I fitted a cfa model with lavaan and try to predict the resulting latent
> variables. I would like to report some descriptive statistics of these
> "new" variables, such as their mean, sd and correlation. However the new
> scale seems to be centered around the mean of 0. E.g. with a min of
> ~-3.5 and a max of ~3.5, instead of 1--7.
> How do I keep the original scale?

The scale of latent variables is arbitrary. We typically assume they are
normally distributed with zero mean, and unit variance.

I would suggest to include the predictors of the latent variables in a
SEM model (instead of extracting the scores to use them elsewhere).

Yves.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: predict(fit) - how can I keep my scale?
parts:
Hi Roman,

Another option is to use a different method of scale setting for the latent variables. Little, Slegers, & Card (2006) describe such a method (and it can be implemented with lavaan).

Alex

Little, T.D., Slegers, D.W., & Card, N.A. (2006). A non-arbitrary method of identifying and scaling latent variables in SEM and MACS models. Structural Equation Modeling, 13, 59–72.

Hi together, 

Thanks for your answers. 

I will used my predictors for the follow-up mediated path model. However since I want to compare different methods of mediation analysis I will need the predicted latent variable scores too. Because I want to report some descriptives of these latent factors I have done the following:

prediction <- predict(fit)
LatentFactor1 <- prediction[,1] + 1 + (((min(prediction[,1]) - max(prediction[,1])) /2)*(-1))

I think that would just move the distribution with its mean value to the center of the scale. Does it do what I think it does?
